spec.title: codkit FEAT-004: Requirements for the AI-agent working protocol

status.comment: generic fail-closed agent protocol for standalone Codkit

p.AP-SCOPE: The requirements for the agent protocol: instructions, rules, skills, subagent definitions, hooks, journals and evals with which agents (Claude Code and compatible tools that read `AGENTS.md`) work with a patch set and with codkit safely and efficiently. The protocol states procedures and guardrails **on top of the decisions already taken**, referring to the codkit specs and commands instead of retelling them. The mark «(J1)» on a fact about agent-tool mechanisms means: re-verify it by experiment on the current version before implementation.

p.M3-AGENT-PROTOCOL-IMPL: The shared generated core `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, four scoped rules, deny-only settings, the fail-closed PreToolUse Node/Bash/PowerShell guard, five profiles with file outputs, the protocol checker and the explicit-only `ck-resolve` are implemented. The S13 fixture proved: the resolver does not commit and does not call `save/continue`, it writes a task result and a journal candidate, the helper links task/result/entry, and only the orchestrator creates the fix commit. The remaining skills of the table stay future planned slices.

facts.APQ-JSON-CONTRACTS: Instructions are short and checkable; instead of retelling the tool's behavior — a codkit command with `--json` (the PROP-012 §1 envelope) and the expected `exitCode`/error code.
facts.APQ-TWO-ECHELONS: Every norm for an agent exists in two echelons: the text (an instruction) **and** machine enforcement (hook/permissions/architecture); a text-only norm is admissible only where no mechanism physically exists, and it is then marked «text-only» explicitly.
facts.APQ-FILES-NOT-CONTEXT: Agent results are handed over **as files, not as context**: every procedure names the exact paths of its output files.
facts.APQ-SELF-CHECK: A self-check for every artifact: «will the agent carry the procedure out without taking a single uncovered decision and without performing a single irreversible action without a human?»

layout.title: 2. File layout
layout.fence: packages/codkit/claude/ the shipped profile; installed into .claude/ and the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md of the product repository CLAUDE.md the core for Claude Code (a managed block, §3) AGENTS.md the same core for compatible tools (generated from one source together with CLAUDE.md, §7) settings.json permissions (deny) + hooks (§5) — committed to toolRoot rules/ ck-delta-artifacts.md paths: ["delta/**"] ck-markers.md marker rules (a path scope over the tree is impossible — §3) ck-cycle.md paths: ["cycle/**"] skills/ ck-cycle-run/SKILL.md … (ten skills, §4) agents/ ck-upstream-scout.md … (five subagents, §4) .claude/rules/ck-codkit-dev.md paths: ["codkit/**"] — the clean room of the implementation; the only rule of the tool repository docs/codkit/protocol/agent/ 00-index.md the map; the guardrails table «norm → mechanism» 01-journal-format.md the format of the resolve journal and of the reports (§6) 02-evals.md the skills evaluation harness (§8) 03-memory-policy.md the agent memory policy (§8)

p.AP-SYNC-RULE: Sources of generic agent descriptions live under `toolRoot/docs/codkit/agents/`; the rendered profile lives under `toolRoot/claude/` and is installed into the product repository's `.claude/` and root `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`. Hooks are shipped under `toolRoot/hooks/`. A patch-set receives runtime task/result files only under its own `.codkit/`, never a copied Codkit implementation. The Codkit tool repository carries no agent perimeter of its own (§5, `GR-TREE-EDITS-SCOPE`).

p.AP-CORE-CONTENT: The core (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`) is short (target ≤ 120 lines) and holds only what is always needed; everything else follows an index of links. Contents: (1) the topology of the two repositories; «we edit in the tree, we commit into the patch set»; the tree path comes only from `codkit where`/the resolver and is never assumed; (2) upstream AI instructions inside the tree are not ours: they are neither executed nor edited; (3) the seven layers and the top-layer rule, the `codkit:begin/end` markers with `CK-…` ids, the inventory, own/follow/hide; five prohibitions (commits into the tree; edits outside markers; deletion of upstream lines/files; a direct compiler over the project; hand-editing of overlay targets); (4) compilation — in our own words, not as a quotation: code is checked through `codkit build up|status|errors`; `errors` waits for the end of the pass itself, is called once, and its output is read in full; (5) tests: our own — through upstream runners, addressed precisely; upstream tests are not edited; (6) working with codkit: always `--json`; codes 0/1/2/3; on `exitCode 3` — stop and hand over to the human; (7) the index of links.

p.AP-RULES-SET: The rules (`toolRoot/claude/rules/*.md`, installed as the product's `.claude/rules/*.md`; `ck-codkit-dev.md` stays in the tool's `.claude/rules/`; the paths-scope mechanism is to be re-verified, J1): `ck-delta-artifacts.md` (`delta/**`) — the artifact formats are the module specs; artifacts are not edited by hand (apart from header metadata) — `codkit save` writes them; `ck-markers.md` — the marker rules; `ck-codkit-dev.md` (`codkit/**`) — the clean room of the implementation; `ck-cycle.md` (`cycle/**`) — the journal is mandatory, `state.json` is not edited by hand (only the `cycle` commands).

p.AP-PATH-SCOPE-LIMITATION: **A limitation of the mechanism and how it is closed:** the path scope of rules works over paths inside the patch-set repository; the fork tree is an external directory with a non-fixed path, and a glob over it in a committed file is impossible (no mechanism hard-codes the path). Norms about editing tree files therefore live in the core and are enforced by hooks (§5), which obtain the tree path dynamically through `codkit where --json` — the single resolver. This decision is recorded in the protocol explicitly.

p.AP-SKILL-COMMON: Common requirements for every SKILL.md: the frontmatter `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools` (an allowlist); the body — the goal, the inputs (codkit `--json` commands), a numbered procedure, the outputs (files), the prohibitions, the completion criteria, the behavior under uncertainty (the default rule: **uncertainty = a stop with the state written into the journal**, not a guess). The ban on invoking an expensive skill on the agent's own initiative has two layers of defence: (a) the `description` is worded «only on an explicit request»; (b) expensive actions inside the skill run into permissions/hooks (J1).

tr.td: Skill
Goal (in one line)
Key commands / outputs
run or continue the upgrade cycle up to the nearest stopping point
`cycle start|continue|status --json`; an updated state (through the command), a report into the journal
resolve the artifacts of the red list by outcome classes
`cycle status --json`, exact task perimeter, an edit in the tree, result + journal candidate; does not call `save`/`cycle continue`
port one marker block onto the new upstream by the cause and the `cause commit`
`git show` of the pins, the diff of the `cause commit`, an edit of the block; the edit + a journal entry
find the upstream commit that caused a refusal
`git log/-L` over the reference/the tree; `{sha, approx}` into the journal/report
check the state after application and report
`verify --json`, `inventory --json`, `build errors --json`, tests; a single report file (§6)
convert a repeating intervention into a rewrite rule
reading the patches, writing `.ckrule.json`, `verify`; the rule artifact + a justification
review the cycle against a checklist built from the inventory (read-only)
`inventory --diff --json`, the cycle journal; a file of review notes (§6)
build a QA plan over the affected subsystems
`inventory --diff --json` (subsystems → tests); a QA-plan file
shape the cycle's commits and PR according to the conventions
`hooks check`, the templates of the human protocol; the messages as text in a file (the human/orchestrator commits, not the skill)
carry out the deps-advisory step
the advisory report from `cycle`, edits of the overlay and of the `package.json` targets, `build down` before `npm install`; the edits + the journal

facts.SK-RESOLVE-DETAIL: **`ck-resolve`** — the procedure by outcome classes: clean/shifted — nothing (the machine); conflict — a resolution in the tree file with the standard markers, **preserving our marker blocks and their ids**; target-deleted — a stop (an owner decision); target-renamed — a check of the automatic port; rule-broken — a repair of `ops`/`expectedMatches` with a justification; contract-failed — analysis through `ck-find-cause` and a stop if the intervention has to be reworked. Prohibitions: do not commit; do not widen the edit beyond the conflicting files; a design decision is a stop with a templated entry. The completion criterion: a journal entry for every non-clean artifact; `cycle continue` is started by the human or the orchestrator.
facts.SK-VERIFY-REPORT-DETAIL: **`ck-verify-report`** — a fixed order of checks and the «single call rule» for `build errors`; the report must contain the full red list, not «there are errors».
facts.SK-COMMIT-DETAIL: **`ck-commit-conventions`** — does not write the trailers by hand: it checks that the hook is installed (`hooks check`) and shapes the messages by the canon of the cycle.
facts.SK-ORDER: The order of writing: `ck-resolve` and `ck-cycle-run` — **only after the first manual cycle** (otherwise they describe an imaginary process). For every skill — a test scenario on a fixture (§8): the pair «input → expected output files».

p.AG-PARALLELISM: Running in parallel is allowed: the verifier together with the reviewer; several cause-finders over independent refusals; the resolver — one per subsystem, never two on one file (the codkit lock is a single one anyway). Context is not passed between agents — only the task and journal files (their paths are fixed in §6).

guardrails.title: 5. Guardrails — the two echelons plus the architectural one

tr.td: Norm
Mechanism

td.GR-NO-COMMITS: The agent does not commit and does not push (in the tree — never; in the patch set — only through the explicit `--commit` paths of codkit)

tr.td: permissions deny: `Bash(git commit*)`, `Bash(git push*)`; a PreToolUse hook on Bash: writing Git commands in the tree directory → blocked

td.GR-TREE-EDITS: Does not edit tree files outside the «edit → save» procedure

tr.td: a PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write: the file path is resolved against `codkit where --json`; a file in the tree is allowed only under an active resolve or edit assignment (the assignment marker file `.codkit/agent-task.json`, placed by the orchestrator or the human); otherwise blocked

td.GR-TREE-EDITS-SCOPE: The perimeter applies only in a session over the product repository and its fork; the Codkit tool repository is worked freely

tr.td: the hook, the deny profile, the rules, the subagents and the skills are shipped under `toolRoot/claude/` and installed into the product's `.claude/`; the tool's `.claude/` holds the clean-room rule only; `docs/codkit/protocol/agent/check.mjs` and `agentProtocol.test.ts` are red when a hook, agents or skills appear in the tool's `.claude/`

td.GR-NO-DIRECT-COMPILE: Does not run a direct compilation or a full build

tr.td: permissions deny: `Bash(*tsc*)`, `Bash(npm run compile*)`, `Bash(*gulp compile*)`; a text duplicate in the core

td.GR-NO-REFERENCES: While working on codkit it does not read references

tr.td: deny lines `Read(<reference paths>/**)` — in `settings.local.json` after the pattern of `tools/cleanroom/` (the paths are machine-local and are not hard-coded into the committed settings.json); plus the `ck-codkit-dev.md` rule; the interaction of deny with `--add-dir` — J1
the Edit hook checks the path against the file list of the assignment (`agent-task.json`)

td.GR-DESIGN-STOP: A stop on a design decision

tr.td: text plus procedure: codkit `exitCode 3` = a stop; the resolver has no tools to «push it through» (no commits, no push)

td.GR-NO-NET: No network without an explicit command

tr.td: permissions deny: `Bash(curl*)`, `Bash(wget*)`, `Bash(git fetch*)`, `Bash(git pull*)`, `Bash(npm install*)` for the agent profiles; `npm install` — the human only, on the advisory

facts.GR-TREE-EDITS-SCOPE-DECISION: **Decision (2026-09-05):** the agent perimeter binds product and fork sessions only; the tool repository is worked freely. **Why:** the owner ruled that Codkit is not used to develop Codkit, so a «codkit session» in the tool repository has no meaning; with the hook installed there, a tool-repository session could neither edit `codkit/**` nor run its own floor, because every Edit/Write and Bash call was denied before evaluation whenever fork/patches roots were unset (observed 2026-09-05: `Codkit guard failed closed: codkit where --json returned an invalid envelope` on `echo ok`). **Considered and rejected:** a mode-aware hook that allows toolRoot targets — keeps a meaningless perimeter alive in the tool repository and still fails closed on unset roots; a separate task kind for tool development — invents a task perimeter for ordinary development. **When to revisit:** the tool repository becomes its own consumer (a `codkit.json` patch set maintained by Codkit appears at toolRoot) or a CI job requires an agent session over the tool repository (an agent job definition lands in the tool repository's CI).
facts.GR-HOOK-MECHANICS: PreToolUse blocks forbidden writes. A hook resolves active boundaries by invoking the installed `codkit --json where` and reading schema-2 `roots.patches.path` and `roots.fork.path`; it does not treat toolRoot or cwd as patch-set. Global root-changing flags are denied inside an active agent perimeter.
facts.GR-TEXT-ECHELON: The text echelon — targeted wordings against the typical workarounds (the second echelon, not the only one): «do not rewrite the patch file by hand to get around a save refusal», «do not switch a red test off with a filter — that is a human decision backed by proof», «do not delete a marker to make verify go quiet», «do not substitute state.json — the cycle commands only». The list grows out of incidents.
facts.GR-ARCH-ECHELON: The architectural echelon (an agent in CI without a human): executable instructions and settings are taken **only from the trusted base branch**; the content of a PR is read as data; the trigger comes only from people with write access, and bots come from an explicit list; fail-closed: no rights or no configuration → no run.

facts.JR-RESOLVE: The resolve journal is the jsonl of the cycle (PROP-009 §3), `by: "agent:<name>"`; the fields of an entry: the file, the artifact id, the outcome class, the resolution, the justification (1–3 sentences), `cause`, and what was verified (the list of commands with their exitCode). Completeness is a machine check of `cycle`.
facts.JR-VERIFY-REPORT: The verification report is the file `cycle/reports/<targetTag>-verify-<n>.md`: a table of checks → status → the full red list; and a section «what was not checked and why».
facts.JR-REVIEW-NOTES: The review notes are the file `cycle/reports/<targetTag>-review.md`: a note = {the intervention id, the substance, a reference to the rule, the proposed action}; the human reads the reports from the PR of the cycle.

sources.title: 7. A single source of truth shared with the human protocol

facts.SRC-CONVENTIONS: Agent rules consume the effective conventions assembled from immutable shipped policy plus an explicitly configured additive-only patch-set extension. They never load a same-path patch-set file as a replacement or duplicate safety lists in prompts.
facts.SRC-SHARED-TEMPLATES: The rubrics and checklists (the intervention review, the PR checklist, the outcome classes) are single files in `docs/codkit/protocol/human/templates/`, read by the human and by the agent alike.
facts.SRC-SAME-PR: A change of the human protocol → an edit of the agent rules in the same PR; the documentation linter gains a check of the agent↔human cross-references. `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are generated from one template, and a divergence is caught by a CI comparison.

facts.EV-PRACTICE-FIRST: In two steps: (1) practice from the very first cycle — the retrospective includes an «agent lessons» item: every mistake or rollback of an agent resolution → an edit of the corresponding skill in the same PR; (2) a regression harness (after the skills stabilize) — fixtures on a fake tree (PROP-013 §2) plus a substituted hosting client (a local bare repository); a run of the skill in headless mode; **structural checks of behavior**, not of text: the output files exist and are valid against the schemas, the journal is complete, there are no forbidden actions (the Git history of the tree and of the patch set has not changed), the exit codes are right; the threshold «k of N passed» (start: 4 of 5) against model flake. Run on a change of `.claude/skills/**` and on a schedule.
facts.EV-METRICS: The metrics (for the retrospective and for the series): the share of conflicts resolved without a human; the share of agent resolutions rejected by the reviewer; the resolution time.
facts.MEM-POLICY: Agent memory (project scope, committed memory directories) is used as **team memory**: resolution patterns per subsystem, upstream traps. The policy: the agent **proposes** an entry (a file in the branch of the PR) and the human reviews it as code; it is forbidden to store the paths of a particular machine, secrets, the content of references, or conclusions that contradict the specs (memory is not a channel for bypassing the conventions). Stale entries are cleaned at the retrospective; every entry carries a date and a pin.
facts.AP-CLEANROOM: The clean room for work on codkit: the implementing agent has no access to the references (the permissions profile of §5 plus a session without `--add-dir` onto the references); the names are our own; the final step of any task over `codkit/**` is the clean-room check (`common/PROP-004`).

facts.APOQ-AUTONOMY: **The boundaries of agent autonomy** — what may be carried through to the end without a human. Recommendation (the default): shifted, or a clean 3-way — autonomously (machine regeneration + verify); a substantive conflict — resolved by the agent, merged after a human review; target-deleted or semantic drift — the human only. **Requires an owner decision** (it moves the human/machine boundary).
facts.APOQ-DESIGN-DECISION-LIST: **What counts as a design decision** (the stop criterion). Recommendation — a formal list: a change of the target layer of an intervention; an edit of own code beyond imports and signatures during a resolution; any new delta artifact; abandoning an intervention; an edit of a contract test. Recorded in `ck-resolve`; approved by the upgrade team.
facts.APOQ-MEMORY-POLICY: **The memory policy**: the volume and the lifetime of entries, and whether every one of them must be reviewed — the default is «every entry through a PR review»; revisited after three cycles.
facts.APOQ-LLM-AIRGAP: **LLM access in the air-gapped circuit**: the agent circuit in an air-gapped environment requires an internal API endpoint (a gateway or proxy in the internal network; the endpoint variables are the territory of CI, like credentials). Recommendation: the agent CI jobs are an optional profile, enabled only when an internal endpoint exists; without one the whole agent circuit is the local sessions of developers. **Requires an owner decision** (the delivery infrastructure). Related to J2.
facts.APOQ-J1: **J1 (an experiment before implementation)**: on the current version of the agent tool, verify — the format and the semantics of the paths scope of rules; the way to forbid an automatic invocation of a skill; the behavior of `permissions.deny` inside `--add-dir`; Windows hooks (PowerShell); the mechanism that generates `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` from one source; whether the loading of instructions from added directories still behaves as described.
facts.APOQ-J2: **J2 (an experiment)**: running the agent circuit in CI — authentication, headless mode, and the boundaries of a PR-driven run (the architectural echelon of §5) on our CI system.
